1	"""Contract §4: the written rule. Deterministic, so anyone can recompute it (label: record)."""
2	import html
3	import re
4	
5	SENIOR = ["Senior", "Sr.", "Staff", "Principal", "Lead", "Director", "Head", "Manager", "III"]
6	STATES = set(("AL AK AZ AR CA CO CT DE FL GA HI ID IL IN IA KS KY LA ME MD MA MI MN MS MO MT NE NV NH NJ NM NY NC ND "
7	              "OH OK OR PA RI SC SD TN TX UT VT VA WA WV WI WY DC").split())
8	CITIZEN = ["U.S. citizen", "US citizen", "United States citizen", "U.S. citizenship", "US citizenship",
9	           "green card", "permanent resident", "security clearance", "ITAR"]
10	EEO = ["regardless of", "without regard to", "discriminate"]
11	NO_SPONSOR = ["will not sponsor", "won't sponsor", "unable to sponsor", "not able to sponsor", "cannot sponsor",
12	              "do not sponsor", "does not sponsor", "not offer sponsorship", "sponsorship is not available",
13	              "sponsorship not available", "without sponsorship", "without the need for sponsorship",
14	              "without requiring sponsorship", "no sponsorship"]
15	YEARS = [r"(\d+)\s*\+\s*years", r"(\d+)\s+or\s+more\s+years", r"at\s+least\s+(\d+)\s+years",
16	         r"minimum\s+of\s+(\d+)\s+years", r"minimum\s+(\d+)\s+years", r"(\d+)\s*(?:-|–|to)\s*\d+\s+years",
17	         r"(\d+)\s+years\s+of"]
18	
19	
20	def plain(content):
21	    """Greenhouse `content` is HTML-escaped HTML: unescape, drop tags, collapse spaces."""
22	    t = html.unescape(html.unescape(content or ""))
23	    t = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", t)
24	    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t).strip()
25	
26	
27	def word_in(needle, text):
28	    return re.search(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])" + re.escape(needle) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])", text, re.I) is not None
29	
30	
31	ABBREV = {"U.S.": "U․S․", "Ph.D.": "Ph․D․", "e.g.": "e․g․", "i.e.": "i․e․"}
32	
33	
34	def sentences(text):
35	    """Split on sentence ends, but not inside 'U.S.', 'Ph.D.', 'e.g.', 'i.e.' (found by test_r5: 'U.S. citizen' was cut in two)."""
36	    for k, v in ABBREV.items():
37	        text = text.replace(k, v)
38	    out = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text)
39	    for k, v in ABBREV.items():
40	        out = [s.replace(v, k) for s in out]
41	    return out
42	
43	
44	def stated_minimums(text):
45	    """Every stated minimum of years. Ranges are read first and masked, so '2-4 years of' gives 2, not also 4
46	    (found by test_r4: the 'N years of' pattern caught the range's upper bound)."""
47	    mins = []
48	    rng = r"(\d+)\s*(?:-|–|to)\s*\d+\s+years"
49	    mins += [int(m) for m in re.findall(rng, text, re.I)]
50	    rest = re.sub(rng, " ", text, flags=re.I)
51	    for pat in YEARS:
52	        if pat == r"(\d+)\s*(?:-|–|to)\s*\d+\s+years":
53	            continue
54	        mins += [int(m) for m in re.findall(pat, rest, re.I)]
55	    return sorted(set(mins))
56	
57	
58	MONTHS = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(["january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july", "august",
59	                                        "september", "october", "november", "december"], 1)}
60	SEASONS = {"spring": 5, "summer": 8, "fall": 12, "autumn": 12, "winter": 2}
61	DATE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(list(MONTHS) + list(SEASONS)) + r")(?:\s*/\s*(?:" + "|".join(SEASONS) + r"))?\s+(20\d\d)\b", re.I)
62	
63	
64	def graduation_window(text):
65	    """R9 (revision 2026-10-30): the posting's graduation window as (start, end) 'YYYY-MM' strings, None if unstated.
66	    A season pair like 'spring/summer 2028' is read at its first season, so the window ends there (stated limit)."""
67	    for s in sentences(text):
68	        low = s.lower()
69	        if "graduat" not in low and not ("complete" in low and "degree" in low):
70	            continue
71	        dates = []
72	        for m in DATE_RE.finditer(s):
73	            word, year = m.group(1).lower(), int(m.group(2))
74	            dates.append(f"{year}-{(MONTHS.get(word) or SEASONS[word]):02d}")
75	        if not dates:
76	            continue
77	        if re.search(r"\bor earlier\b|\bby\b|\bbefore\b", low):
78	            return (None, max(dates))
79	        return (min(dates), max(dates))
80	    return None
81	
82	
83	PROVINCES = set("AB BC MB NB NL NS NT NU ON PE QC SK YT".split())
84	
85	
86	def _segment_is_us(seg):
87	    """R3 for one ';'-separated location segment. Revision 2026-10-30: a segment that also names a Canadian
88	    province (e.g. 'Toronto, ON, CA') reads its trailing CA as Canada, not California."""
89	    if re.search(r"\b(United States|USA|US)\b", seg):
90	        return True
91	    codes = re.findall(r",\s*([A-Z]{2})\b", seg)
92	    if any(c in PROVINCES for c in codes):
93	        return False
94	    return any(c in STATES for c in codes)
95	
96	
97	def _r(check, resume_field, posting_field, ok, evidence):
98	    return {"check": check, "resume_field": resume_field, "posting_field": posting_field,
99	            "result": "pass" if ok else "fail", "evidence": evidence}
100	
101	
102	def judge(posting, resume):
103	    title = posting.get("title", "")
104	    loc = (posting.get("location") or {}).get("name", "")
105	    text = plain(posting.get("content", ""))
106	    wa = resume["work_authorization"]
107	    exp = resume["experience_years"]
108	    out = []
109	
110	    hits = [t for t in resume["target_roles"] if t.lower() in title.lower()]
111	    out.append(_r("R1", "target_roles", "title", bool(hits), f"title '{title}' contains {hits or 'no target role'}"))
112	
113	    if exp < 3:
114	        sen = [w for w in SENIOR if word_in(w, title)]
115	        out.append(_r("R2", "experience_years", "title", not sen, f"title '{title}' senior words: {sen or 'none'}"))
116	    else:
117	        out.append(_r("R2", "experience_years", "title", True, f"does not apply (experience_years={exp})"))
118	
119	    us = any(_segment_is_us(seg) for seg in loc.split(";"))
120	    country_ok = us if wa["country"] == "US" else False
121	    out.append(_r("R3", "work_authorization.country", "location.name", country_ok,
122	                  f"location '{loc}' {'is' if country_ok else 'is not shown to be'} in {wa['country']}"))
123	
124	    if exp < 3:
125	        mins = stated_minimums(text)
126	        over = [m for m in mins if m >= 3]
127	        out.append(_r("R4", "experience_years", "content", not over, f"stated minimum years: {mins or 'none'}"))
128	    else:
129	        out.append(_r("R4", "experience_years", "content", True, f"does not apply (experience_years={exp})"))
130	
131	    if not wa["us_citizen"]:
132	        found = [p for s in sentences(text) if not any(e in s.lower() for e in EEO)
133	                 for p in CITIZEN if word_in(p, s)]   # whole words: 'ITAR' once matched inside 'military'
134	        out.append(_r("R5", "work_authorization.us_citizen", "content", not found, f"citizenship/clearance phrases: {sorted(set(found)) or 'none'}"))
135	    else:
136	        out.append(_r("R5", "work_authorization.us_citizen", "content", True, "does not apply (us_citizen=true)"))
137	
138	    if wa["needs_sponsorship"]:
139	        found = [p for p in NO_SPONSOR if word_in(p, text)]
140	        out.append(_r("R6", "work_authorization.needs_sponsorship", "content", not found, f"no-sponsorship phrases: {found or 'none'}"))
141	    else:
142	        out.append(_r("R6", "work_authorization.needs_sponsorship", "content", True, "does not apply (needs_sponsorship=false)"))
143	
144	    has_phd = any(str(e.get("degree", "")).lower() in ("phd", "ph.d.", "doctorate") for e in resume["education"])
145	    if not has_phd:
146	        req = [s for s in sentences(text)
147	               if re.search(r"\b(PhD|Ph\.D\.|doctorate|doctoral)", s, re.I)
148	               and re.search(r"\b(required|requires|must)\b", s, re.I) and "preferred" not in s.lower()]
149	        out.append(_r("R7", "education[].degree", "content", not req, f"PhD-required sentences: {len(req)}"))
150	    else:
151	        out.append(_r("R7", "education[].degree", "content", True, "does not apply (has a PhD)"))
152	
153	    win = graduation_window(text)
154	    edu = resume["education"][0]
155	    g0, g1 = edu.get("graduation"), edu.get("graduation_latest") or edu.get("graduation")
156	    if win is None or not g0:
157	        out.append(_r("R9", "education[0].graduation", "content", True,
158	                      "no graduation window stated" if win is None else "persona has no graduation date"))
159	    else:
160	        start, end = win
161	        ok = (start is None or g1 >= start) and (end is None or g0 <= end)
162	        out.append(_r("R9", "education[0].graduation", "content", ok,
163	                      f"posting window {start or '…'} to {end or '…'}; persona {g0} to {g1}"))
164	
165	    sk = [s for s in resume["skills"] if word_in(s, text)]
166	    out.append(_r("R8", "skills", "content", len(sk) >= 2, f"résumé skills found in content: {sk}"))
167	
168	    verdict = "relevant" if all(c["result"] == "pass" for c in out) else "not_relevant"
169	    return {"verdict": verdict, "label": "record", "reasons": out}

2	Defect: R3 read only two-letter state codes, so 364 real Databricks postings such as
3	'San Francisco, California' failed R3 (review/01-reproduce-before.txt)."""
4	import json
5	import os
6	import sys
7	import unittest
8	
9	ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
10	sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)
11	from agent import rule  # noqa: E402
12	
13	RESUME = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "persona", "resume.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
14	
15	
16	def r3(loc):
17	    p = {"id": 1, "title": "Data Analyst", "location": {"name": loc}, "content": "SQL and Python"}
18	    return {r["check"]: r for r in rule.judge(p, RESUME)["reasons"]}["R3"]["result"]
19	
20	
21	class R3FullStateNames(unittest.TestCase):
22	    # Yudan's predictions: US
23	    def test_city_and_full_state(self):
24	        self.assertEqual(r3("San Francisco, California"), "pass")
25	        self.assertEqual(r3("New York City, New York"), "pass")
26	
27	    def test_washington_dc(self):
28	        self.assertEqual(r3("Washington, D.C."), "pass")
29	
30	    def test_remote_with_a_state(self):
31	        self.assertEqual(r3("Remote - California"), "pass")
32	
33	    def test_state_name_alone(self):
34	        self.assertEqual(r3("California; New York"), "pass")
35	
36	    # Yudan's predictions: not US
37	    def test_georgia_the_country(self):
38	        self.assertEqual(r3("Tbilisi, Georgia"), "fail")
39	
40	    def test_other_countries(self):
41	        for loc in ("Toronto, Canada", "London, United Kingdom", "Bengaluru, India"):
42	            self.assertEqual(r3(loc), "fail", loc)
43	
44	    # unchanged from JS1 (regression)
45	    def test_js1_behaviour_kept(self):
46	        self.assertEqual(r3("San Francisco, CA"), "pass")
47	        self.assertEqual(r3("Toronto, ON, CA"), "fail")
48	        self.assertEqual(r3("Remote"), "fail")
49	
50	    def test_state_name_inside_another_word_does_not_count(self):
51	        self.assertEqual(r3("Indianapolis Avenue, London, United Kingdom"), "fail")
52	
53	
54	if __name__ == "__main__":
55	    unittest.main()

**The change:** I added a list of full state names, `STATE_NAMES`, which includes "District of Columbia" and "D.C.". `_segment_is_us` now also passes a location segment that contains one of those names as a whole word, using the existing `word_in` helper. The order of checks is the same as before: "United States"/"USA"/"US" first, then the Canadian province check, then state codes, and only then the full names.

**How the test cases come out:**
- **Pass:** "San Francisco, California", "New York City, New York", "Remote - California" and "California; New York" all now pass because they contain a state name. "Washington, D.C." passes on "Washington" (and on "D.C.").
- **Still fail:**
  - "Indianapolis Avenue, …" fails because "Indiana" only counts as a whole word.
  - "Bengaluru, India" fails because "India" is not "Indiana".
  - "Toronto, Canada", "London, United Kingdom" and "Remote" fail because they contain no state name.
- **Old behaviour kept:** the two-letter codes and the province case ("Toronto, ON, CA") work exactly as before. The R3 tests in `tests/test_contract.py` still give the same results.

**One limit to know about:** I left Georgia out of the list, because otherwise "Tbilisi, Georgia" would pass as a US location. The cost is that "Atlanta, Georgia" now fails R3 unless the location also says "GA" or "US". A comment above the list says this.
